paper_design_summary: A system paper on Varif.ai, a text-to-image tool (SD-XL Lightning plus LLaMA-2) that lets users verify and vary attribute distributions in a generated image set. After an 8-person elicitation study and an 8-person formative study (qualitative, no comparison group), a summative lab study over Zoom had 20 participants generate diverse image sets with Varif.ai and with a Prompt-only version of the same tool, within subjects in counterbalanced random order, with the scenario (Doctors, Birds, Cars) randomly assigned between subjects. The main scored outcome is the CLIP-embedding diversity span of each participant's own image collection.

studies.label: Summative user study (Varif.ai vs Prompt-only image generation)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two techniques (Prompt-only then Varif.ai, or the reverse) for the open-ended task; scenario (Doctors, Birds, Cars) assigned between subjects
assignment.quote: Generate images iteratively for the Open-ended degree of specification using Prompt-only, then Varif.ai (or in reversed depending on random assignment).
assignment.locator: p. 10, Section 7.1.2 Procedure; also p. 9, Section 7.1.1 ("within-subjects with counterbalancing")

arms.name: Varif.ai
arms.description: Full tool: prompt entry plus Attributes tab with LLM-suggested labels and editable histograms that set label proportions in probabilistic prompts

arms.name: Prompt-only
arms.description: Ablated version of Varif.ai with only the prompt text entry and no Attributes tab

participants.exclusions: None reported. The paper gives one count (20 recruited); Fig. 11 (p. 12) shows 20 distinct participant IDs (6 Doctors, 7 Birds, 7 Cars). Each participant used both techniques, so each arm has the same 20 people.
participants.who: Adults aged 21 to 33 (median 23), 12 female, recruited through a local university mailing list and mutual connections; backgrounds in social sciences, medicine, arts, business, and STEM; nine had no prior text-to-image experience
participants.quote: We recruited 20 participants through a local university mailing list and mutual connections. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 33 (Median = 23), were 12 female, and had diverse educational backgrounds

ai_tool.name_model: Varif.ai built on SD-XL Lightning (text-to-image) and LLaMA-2 (label suggestions), CLIP for image labeling
ai_tool.how_used: Participants iteratively generated image sets from prompts; in the Varif.ai arm they also added attributes and adjusted label distributions

task.description: Generate a diverse set of reference images for an assigned scenario (kid book illustrator portraying doctors, teacher showing bird variety, car poster references), first with an open-ended diversity goal; Varif.ai alone was then used for attribute-specific and attribute-label-specific goals
task.duration: Main session 40 min within a one-hour Zoom session

outcomes.name: Computed image diversity (span) of the participant's image collection, open-ended goal
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Diversity span (95th percentile of distances of CLIP ViT-bigG-14 image embeddings from their mean) over each participant's collection, augmented to 50 images with the original attribute specification. Variety within one person's own image set, not across people; coded flexibility under the codebook rule. Linear mixed-effects models with post-hoc contrasts.

contrasts.reported: Varif.ai span mean M = 0.65 vs Prompt-only M = 0.45; p < .0001 (also vs Original, no user interaction, M = 0.35; p < .0001). Fig. 8a shows 90% confidence intervals.

eligibility.reason: Randomized within-person experiment (counterbalanced order, random assignment stated) comparing two generative-AI configurations, with an embedding-based diversity score on each participant's own image set. Only 20 people took part (p. 10), well below 50, so it goes to the screening report as a small randomized experiment. The other two studies (8 people each) are qualitative with no comparison group. The diversity outcome is within one person's set, not across people.

one_line_finding: In a within-person experiment with 20 participants, image sets made with Varif.ai had a higher CLIP diversity span than those made with the Prompt-only version (M = 0.65 vs 0.45, p < .0001; p. 11, Section 7.2.1 and Fig. 8a).

applied.locator: p. 2, footnote 1; also p. 7, Section 5.4 (Implementation Details)
